inline_comments.comment: Using `withToolbar || !!onReloadStory` means the toolbar is forced visible whenever `onReloadStory` is provided, even if the user has explicitly set `withToolbar: false` (via prop or `parameters.docs.canvas.withToolbar: false`). Since `onReloadStory` is unconditionally passed for all inline stories from Canvas.tsx, users currently have no way to opt out of this toolbar. Consider respecting an explicit opt-out, e.g. only forcing the toolbar on when `withToolbar !== false`, or exposing a `withReloadButton` prop on `CanvasProps` that defaults to `true` but can be disabled.

Same concern as the `PreviewContainer` spread above: the condition `withToolbar || onReloadStory` renders the toolbar even when `withToolbar` has been explicitly set to `false`. These two sites need to be kept in sync and should reflect the same opt-out logic.

There is currently no way for a story author to opt out of the reload button for a specific inline story. The PR description says the button is shown by default for all inline stories, but the lack of a corresponding `withReloadButton` (or similar) parameter means this is an all-or-nothing feature. If configuration parity with `withToolbar` (which supports `parameters.docs.canvas.withToolbar`) is desirable, that would need to be added here.

The `key="reload"` prop on the `Button` element is unnecessary. `key` is only meaningful when React needs to reconcile a list of sibling elements produced by `.map()` or an array literal. Here the element is a single conditional child inside a fragment, so the `key` has no effect and can be removed.

The existing manager-level remount tool (`code/core/src/manager/components/preview/tools/remount.tsx`) provides animation feedback by spinning the `SyncIcon` on click and listening for the `FORCE_REMOUNT` event to reset the state. This implementation has no such feedback, so the button gives no visual indication that the action was triggered. Adding a brief animation (even a simple CSS rotation on click) would keep the two reload controls consistent in UX.

general_comments.comment: No new Storybook stories have been added for the `onReloadStory` prop. `Preview.stories.tsx` already has a rich set of `WithToolbar*` stories that demonstrate toolbar variants; a similar story (e.g. `WithReloadStory`) showing the new button in isolation would make the feature self-documenting and easier to visually regression-test.

The documentation file `docs/api/doc-blocks/doc-block-canvas.mdx` is not updated to mention the new automatic reload button. Readers who consult the Canvas doc-block reference will have no way to know the button exists, how it behaves, or how (if ever) they can suppress it. The PR checklist also has the documentation box unchecked.
